editorial.headline: Electrical Control Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 27120 covers the industrial manufacture of electrical control and distribution equipment, with full national PMA openness but a Bali registration block for PMA.
editorial.body:
KBLI 27120 is a manufacturing code for the hardware that controls, protects, switches, and distributes electrical power. Its scope includes voltage regulators, circuit breakers, surge suppressors for distribution-voltage systems, control panels for power distribution, switchgear and its components, automatic control panels, lighting distribution boards, control desks, electrical relays, switchboard conduits or channels, fuses, power-switching equipment, electrical power switches, and kWh meters.

In practical terms, this is not a trading or installation activity. It is the factory-side production of the apparatus that sits inside electrical distribution systems: the boards, relays, breakers, regulators, switches, fuses, and metering equipment that make power controllable and interruptible. The record also draws the boundary by exclusion, keeping this activity focused on control and distribution equipment rather than other electrical, process-control, generator, soldering, converter, or combustion-engine starter equipment.

The national investment picture is straightforward. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That means the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. The activity is also open across all listed operating scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. For a founder reading the code nationally, the signal is broad: this is an industrial manufacturing activity that can be registered at any of those scales, and the national PMA line is open up to full foreign ownership.

Bali changes the answer. The same slim record marks the Bali status as Blocked (risk class) and sets l4_bali_blocked to true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and therefore the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium from May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is categorical: Bali province blocks ALL Low + Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest reading is this: nationally, KBLI 27120 is foreign-open; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register it for PMA today under the Bali-side block described in the record.
